0.0.n: Refers to this video or presentation, rather than necessarily today.

0.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic of the sentence.

0.2.n: Here, です adds politeness to the opening rather than stating that something is something else.

0.3.n: Softens the opening and gently draws the listener in.

0.5.n: セ is the first part of セリア, the name of a Japanese discount store.

0.6.n: リア completes the store name セリア; it is not a separate word here.

0.7.n: Marks セリア as the place where the purchases happened.

0.8.n: 購入した is the past form of 購入する and describes the 商品 that follow.

0.9.n: Refers to the products the speaker purchased.

0.10.n: Links 商品 to 紹介, showing what will be introduced.

0.11.n: Used with をする to describe presenting the purchased items.

0.12.n: Marks 紹介 as the activity carried out with する.

0.13.m: want to go ahead and do
0.13.n: する becomes して, followed by いく for proceeding and たい for wanting to do something.

0.14.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

0.15.n: The polite form of 思う; after たいと, it makes the speaker’s intention sound softer.

1.0.n: Used at the start to connect this sentence to the previous explanation.

1.2.n: 約 makes the number approximate, and 点 counts individual items or products.

1.3.n: The て-form of ある connects the item count to the next description.

1.5.n: シール refers to adhesive decorations here, not an official seal.

1.6.n: Lists examples without implying these are the only types of items.

1.7.n: Combines with もの to form 紙もの, a term for paper goods.

1.8.n: Combines with 紙 to refer to paper-based items, such as decorative stationery.

1.9.n: Marks stickers and paper goods as what the following description applies to.

1.10.n: Adding め to 多い suggests a relatively large amount without giving an exact proportion.

1.11.n: Links 多め to なる, marking the resulting state.

1.12.n: なる uses ている in polite form to describe the resulting makeup of the selection.

2.0.n: Signals a transition from the introduction to the main activity.

2.2.n: 始める becomes 始めて, followed by いきましょう, a polite invitation to proceed.

0.lit: This time, you see, at Seria bought items’ introduction I want to go ahead and do, I think.
0.tip: 購入した comes before 商品: Japanese puts the description bought at Seria directly before items.

1.lit: And, about thirty items there are, and stickers and paper goods are on the plentiful side.
1.tip: や lists examples, so stickers and paper goods are not necessarily the only categories.

2.lit: Well then, right away, let’s go ahead and start.
2.tip: ましょう politely invites the listener to join in: let’s do something.
